summary.title: Implicit structural absorption without explicit citation
summary.description: This example represents a case where a later work appears to absorb or reproduce structural features of an earlier source without explicit citation or acknowledgement.

trace_claim.claim_statement: The later work appears to reflect structural influence from the earlier source, but no explicit citation is present.

derived_or_later_work.title: Later Work With Similar Structural Pattern
derived_or_later_work.creator: Later Creator

evidence_items.description: The later work uses a similar layered structure, progression, and conceptual ordering to the earlier source.
observed_features: similar separation between observation, review, and allocation
similar distinction between trace and judgment

evidence_items.description: The later work appears to reuse a similar conceptual distinction without direct citation.
observed_features: allocation is treated as a downstream process

evidence_items.description: No direct citation, acknowledgement, or reference to the origin candidate is present in the later work.

evidence.evidence_summary: The later work shows structural and conceptual similarity to the origin candidate, but no explicit citation is present.

audit_assessment.assessment_summary: There is moderate evidence of structural absorption, but the absence of explicit citation prevents a direct source-reference conclusion.
uncertainty_notes: Structural similarity may result from shared context, common discourse, parallel development, or indirect influence.
The audit does not prove copying, plagiarism, ownership, or legal infringement.
The relationship should be treated as a trace hypothesis rather than a verdict.
Further review is required before any dispute or allocation process.

review_notes: Reviewers should compare structural features rather than isolated wording.
Reviewers should consider the possibility of common background knowledge.
Reviewers should avoid treating similarity as proof of intentional use.
This case is suitable for multi-wing review if downstream dispute or allocation is considered.

dispute_notes: No formal dispute has been registered in this example.
If challenged by either party, this example may be escalated to a Dispute Registry.

allocation_readiness.reason: Implicit absorption is not sufficient for allocation without additional review, stronger evidence, and dispute-status clarification.
allocation_readiness.recommended_next_step: Conduct a structured review comparing the origin candidate and later work across multiple trace dimensions.

governance_notes.principle: Implicit absorption may be observed as a trace hypothesis, but it must not be treated as a final judgment.
